title: Wishing for Peace
subtitle: Please don't forget every dove that flies your way—and the olive branches they carry from afar.

trails.title: Pure White Folder
trails.description: Humanity has always known how to survive adversity.

content.text:
Arcana Invasion Assessment Report

The following is a strategic analysis and operational assessment of the recent Arcana invasion:

I. Assessment of Strategic Intent
Arcana's invasion was not aimed at territorial or resource expansion—it was a strategic probe. Her core intentions are assessed as follows:
1. To draw out the Pax House and force it to expose its operational movements under pressure.
2. To test the Core Guard's combat effectiveness and collect critical data on our core security forces.

II. Current Situation and Response Assessment
The Core Guard has demonstrated loyalty and effectiveness, but its premature entry into direct combat has resulted in the following consequences:
1. Our strategic cards were shown too early—the Core Guard's true capabilities and tactical characteristics may now be known to the enemy.
2. Strategic initiative has been partially ceded. We will face targeted countermeasures going forward, while the enemy still holds options in reserve.

III. Conclusions and Recommendations
This confrontation has allowed Arcana to partially achieve her strategic objectives. We recommend the following:
1. Reassess the threshold for deploying the Core Guard to avoid depleting strategic reserves in response to low-cost probes.
2. Apply tactical deception and upgrades to the Core Guard—projecting a false profile alongside the real one to mislead the enemy.
3. Establish a tiered response framework that clearly defines the escalation order of the Foundation's defense forces, Zeno forces, and the Core Guard.

items.text: Wishing for Peace
Countdown to the "Storm"
Time and fate ceaselessly intertwine.
Time is a metaphor for fate.
The past is dead and gone. The present is but a fleeting moment trapped within a tiny crevice. And the future ...
And the future revealed itself before me.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Can you hear me, Timekeeper?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I ... Sonetto?

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Timekeeper, I'm here.
Golden threads coil all around. All sense of direction is lost.
Reach out a hand and—

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: I've got you.

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: The jumbled timeline contracts, and a familiar starting place takes form.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: What just happened? What did you see in there?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: We did it, Sonetto.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Did what?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Arcana has retreated.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: You confronted her in there?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: She spoke to me. She said, "Welcome back."

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I tried to dispel the mist around her, but then she just disappeared.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: It doesn't feel right. I don't understand what I did.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: We'll figure it out some day. Whatever you did, it must have been powerful.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Yes, we can figure things out later. Let's just find a way back first.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Do you know where we are?

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: I think we're back in the library. This is the same study room we left before going to the central tower.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Hello?
Images and sounds flood in from all directions, condensing and taking a new shape. And in that space, a gleaming silhouette manifests.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: What's that?
She hears a familiar voice.
"It's an item Igor gave me during the Don Operation."
"It's possible that it could generate an immunity zone. But ..."

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: It's us, Timekeeper, and Merel, back when we were discussing whether to open the "boon."

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Then, they're about to ...
Just as expected, the dark gate appears once more.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: They're going through the gate, or we are.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I know how to get out. Sonetto, lead me to the gate.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Right. Stay close.
But the gate seems to exert a powerful repulsive force.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: It won't open from this side. Just as I thought.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: The gate can only be opened from the other side. Someone has to come in first.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Come in, Sonetto. Vertin, you have to bring Sonetto with you.
At first, it isn't clear whether the voice can travel through the gate, but then, memories provide an answer.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: We're just about to enter through the gate.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Which means we need to leave at the same time.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: I'm ready.
She waits until the very moment that past and future converge.
"We meet here again before the 'Storm.' And whatever happens, we move forward together."
"Mhm. I promise."
"It's time. Let's go, Sonetto."

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Now, Timekeeper!
Past and present selves brush shoulders. The loop is closed.
Dust appears and sweeps everything away once more. Darkness and silence flood all senses.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Sonetto?

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: I'm here. We're back to our real ages. How's your eyesight, Timekeeper?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I can see again. It seems we've made it back to reality.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Finally!
The dark gate at the center of the room disappears, and in its place, shrunk down to its original form, appears the floating black box.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: But there's only three minutes left before the "Storm."

items.speaker: Lavender
items.text: Ah, Ms. Vertin, Ms. Sonetto!

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Lavender?

items.speaker: Lavender
items.text: I heard voices. Thank goodness you're back.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: How's everything in the library? Is everyone alright?

items.speaker: Lavender
items.text: For now ...
Lavender walks out toward the main hall.
The students are huddled in the book storage area outside the study room.

items.speaker: Emilia
items.text: The Doves aren't glowing so much anymore.
Yet they guard them in silence all the same.
They've brought Matilda here, too. A Shelter Dove casts a faint glow on her still-unconscious form.

items.speaker: Lavender
items.text: The immunity zone has shrunk so far that it doesn't cover the library anymore. We'd all have been doomed if these two students hadn't brought us these backup Shelter Doves.

items.speaker: Lavender
items.text: They said Ms. Merel was the one who got them.

items.speaker: Lavender
items.text: But the Doves may not last long. Without them ...

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Things will be alright now, Lavender.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I've found a shelter strong enough for all of us.
This isn't the first time she's seen the "Storm" as it arrives.
But there's something different this time. As the world shatters before her eyes, she's without a safe place to hide or an Equilibrium Umbrella.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: The rain ... It's rising.
The wave of adrenaline is receding. Her wounded legs cry out their refusal in her sprint between her and the library.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Heh heh!

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Who? Who's there?

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Vertin and Sonetto made it.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: We're going to be okay. Come on.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: They made it? But ...

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: But what? They can save everyone, us included. Come! Come!

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: I can't go any further.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: The reverse has already started. It's too late.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: I'm just hallucinating. You're not real. This must be the Storm Syndrome.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Don't give up now, Merel.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: You can make it. Just give it everything. If you do, we all live.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Keep your head up. Look.
She forces her head up. The rain swirls everything into a blur, but she makes out buildings burning and trees, walls—even the sky itself—being ripped apart.
Yet part of the library doesn't yield. She sees light pouring out from the doors and windows.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: It's so far.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: This is where I failed my first PE test. I just couldn't reach the end of the track in time.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: But you've grown up. You're not that little girl anymore.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Come on, Merel. Move your feet.

items.speaker: Lavender
items.text: Everyone, stay together. Don't leave the light.

items.speaker: Lavender
items.text: Gather around Ms. Vertin.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Merel?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Where's Merel?

items.speaker: Merel?
items.text: Keep going. Just a little more.

items.speaker: Merel?
items.text: It's so close. We can make it.

items.speaker: Merel?
items.text: We still have a promise to keep. Remember?

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Vertin ... Sonetto ...

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Is that Merel?

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Just a little bit closer.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: I don't want to go.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Don't leave me, Vert—

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Merel! No!
